questions.question: What do we mean by Allen’s rule?

options.text: Mammals from colder climates generally have shorter ears and limbs to minimise heat loss.
Desert lizards lack the physiological ability that mammals have to deal with the high temperatures of their habitat.
Some plants have no leaves – they are reduced to spines – and the photosynthetic function is taken over by the flattened stems.
The body compensates low oxygen availability by increasing red blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing the breathing rate.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 1**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Allen's Rule is a principle in biology which suggests that animals living in colder regions tend to have shorter appendages (such as ears, tails, and limbs) to conserve body heat, while animals in warmer climates tend to have longer appendages to dissipate excess heat. 
 
• This adaptation helps maintain thermal balance by reducing the surface area through which heat can be lost in colder environments and increasing it in hotter environments to release heat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Statement 2 

 
 
• Describes adaptations to high temperatures, but it is not Allen's Rule.
 
 
 
• Statement 3 
 
 
• Refers to adaptations in desert plants, such as succulents, not Allen's Rule.
 
 
 
• Statement 4 
 
 
• Describes physiological responses to high-altitude environments, such as increased red blood cell production, but again, this is unrelated to Allen's Rule.

questions.question: The Mahalanobis model was the basis for which Five-Year Plan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Second Five-yea Plan**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Mahalanobis model was the basis for the Second Five-Year Plan of India, which took place from 1956–1961: 
 
• The Mahalanobis model was an economic development model created by Indian statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis in 1953.
 
• The model was based on an input-output model and was used to establish the plan's goals and priorities.
 
• The plan's goals included: Rapid industrialization, Development of the public sector, Balanced allocation of investment between productive sectors, and A 25% increase in national income. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Second Five-Year Plan
 
 
• The Second Five-Year Plan in India was from 1956 to 1961.
 
• The plan's main objectives were to develop heavy industries and construct railway lines in the northeast. 
 
 
 
• Sixth Five-Year Plan
 
 
• The Sixth Five-Year Plan in India was from 1980 to 1985.
 
• The plan's objectives were to increase national income, modernize technology, and reduce poverty and unemployment. 
 
 
 
• First Five-Year Plan
 
 
• The First Five-Year Plan in India was from 1951 to 1956.
 
• The plan was based on the Harrod-Domar Model and focused on agriculture.

questions.question: Which of the following types of unemployment is found in India when people are employed for a certain period of a year in tourist resorts and various tourism-related activities in the mountain regions, but are unemployed in off-seasons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seasonal unemployment**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Seasonal unemployment is the type of unemployment that occurs when people are employed for a certain period of the year but are unemployed during other times.
 
• This is the type of unemployment that occurs in India when people are employed in the tourism sector but are unemployed during the off-season. 
 
• Seasonal unemployment is common in industries and occupations that are subject to seasonal demand or weather, such as tourism, farming, and construction.
 
• In the tourism sector, some months of the year have more tourists than others, which can lead to seasonal unemployment. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other types of unemployment include:
 
• Frictional unemployment: Occurs when someone is unemployed by choice while looking for a better job opportunity. 
 
• Underemployment
 
 
• When people are employed but want or are available to work more hours.
 
• This can include part-time workers who want to work full-time or people who usually work full-time but are currently working part-time. 
 
 
 
• Disguised unemployment
 
 
• When people are employed but not to their full potential due to a lack of opportunities.
 
• This can include people who are working below their skill set, or people who are doing part-time work but want to work full-time.
 
• Disguised unemployment is also known as underemployment
 
 
 
• Cyclical unemployment is a type of unemployment that occurs when the economy changes, such as during a recession or period of economic growth.
 
 
• It's characterized by a short-term increase in unemployment, usually lasting from one month to 1.5 years.

questions.question: According to which of the following foreign travellers, people of Delhi used to write letters containing abuses to the Sultan, therefore, in order to punish them Sultan decided to shift the capital?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ibn Batuta**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ibn Batuta visited India during the reign of Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
 
• According to his accounts, the people of Delhi used to write letters containing abuses to the Sultan.
 
• To punish them, the Sultan decided to shift the capital from Delhi to Devagiri, which he renamed as Daulatabad.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hasan Nizami:
 
 
• Hasan Nizami was a Persian historian and writer during the medieval period.
 
• He is best known for his work, "Taj-ul-Maasir", a historical account of the reign of the Sultan of Delhi, Mahmud of Ghazni.
 
• Nizami's work offers valuable insights into the politics, culture, and social conditions of that period.
 
 
 
• Al-Biruni:
 
 
• Abu Rayhan al-Biruni (973–1048) was a renowned Persian scholar, historian, and polymath during the Islamic Golden Age.
 
• He made significant contributions to many fields, including astronomy, mathematics, physics, and geography.
 
• Al-Biruni is especially famous for his works on India, including "Kitab al-Hind", in which he detailed the culture, religion, and sciences of India.
 
• His scholarly approach combined a deep understanding of Indian civilization with a critical and comparative analysis.
 
 
 
• Isami:
 
 
• Isami (also known as Siyah-yi Isami) was a Persian historian and author who lived during the 14th century.
 
• He is best known for his historical work "Futuh al-Salatin" (The Conquests of Kings), which provides an account of the history of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• His work is a valuable source for understanding the history of medieval India, particularly during the reign of the early Sultans

questions.question: How long will a sound wave take to travel 1.5km, which has a frequency of 5 kHz and wavelength of 6 cm?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 seconds**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• To calculate the time it takes for a sound wave to travel a distance, we can use the formula:

 
 
• ​Distance/ Speed of Sound
 
 
 
• We are given:
 
 
• Distance = 1.5 km = 1500 meters
 
 
 
• Frequency of the sound wave = 5 kHz = 5000 Hz
 
 
• Wavelength = 6 cm = 0.06 meters
 
 
 
• First, we need to calculate the speed of sound using the formula:
 
 
• Speed of sound=Frequency×Wavelength
 
 
 
• Substituting the given values:
 
 
• ​Speed of sound=5000Hz×0.06m=300m/s
 
 
 
• Now, we can calculate the time taken for the sound wave to travel 1500 meters:
 
 
• ​Time= 1500m/300m/s=5 Seconds

The correct answer is__** Kushana**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Vasudeva I was one of the prominent rulers of the Kushana dynasty,** which ruled over a large part of northern India and Central Asia from the 1st to 3rd centuries CE.
 
• The** Kushana Empire is known for its cultural and economic achievements, including the introduction of gold coins.**
